snapshot.fact: FY2025 earnings $28.8B ($30.1B ex-identified items); sales and other operating revenue $323.9B; total revenues and other income $332.2B; operating cash flow $52.0B; free cash flow $26.1B.
FY2025 net production averaged 4.7M oil-equivalent barrels/day, highest in more than 40 years.
~58,000 regular employees at YE2025, down from 61,000 (2024) and 62,000 (2023); over 59% outside the U.S.
Businesses: Upstream, Product Solutions (Energy Products, Chemical Products, Specialty Products) and Low Carbon Solutions.
2030 Plan (Dec 2025): +$25B earnings and +$35B cash flow growth vs 2024 with no capital increase; ROCE >17% in 2030; ~$145B cumulative surplus cash through 2030 at $65 Brent.
Structural cost savings target raised to $20B cumulative vs 2019 by 2030; drivers explicitly include operational efficiencies and workforce reductions.
Upstream targets 5.5M boe/d by 2030; Permian roughly doubling to ~2.5M boe/d; advantaged assets (Permian, Guyana, LNG) ~65% of volumes; ~$20B lower-emission investment 2025-2030.
CEO Darren Woods frames the transformation as delivering a 'technology-led business with structurally stronger earnings power'.
Q2 2026 earnings $14.5B; operating cash flow $23.6B; record Permian >1.8M boe/d; cumulative structural cost savings $16.3B vs 2019 ($1.2B in 1H26); YTD capex $13.0B.

tech_posture.fact: Consolidating 12 ERP systems into a single SAP S/4HANA instance, targeted for 2028; CEO says it is 'already delivering results'; 97% fewer profit centres, 70% fewer cost centres.

Legacy SAP ECC6 estate carries ~65 million lines of custom code (CFO called it a record among SAP customers); program also replaces a decades-old mainframe for consolidation across ~1,000 legal entities; unified ERP initiative started 2023, fit-to-standard approach.

Global Business Solutions (GBS) owns end-to-end processes and the AI + process automation agenda; uses Celonis process intelligence (procurement, supply chain, maintenance, AP/AR) including to support the ECC6-to-S/4HANA migration. ExxonMobil is a large AWS customer and uses Snowflake.
Central Data Office (created May 2023, moved out of IT, reports into Global Business Solutions / Transformation Enablement) built a consolidated enterprise data ecosystem on Snowflake.
Long-term agreement with Cerebre to accelerate ExxonMobil's 'Foundational Digital Backbone' (operational data / industrial knowledge graph).

IT reorganized from 2022 into centralized service delivery groups; Global Business Centers in Budapest, Bengaluru and Buenos Aires; job postings cite ServiceNow, Kubernetes, SailPoint, DevOps 'secrets engineers'; IT priorities include several major ERP migrations.
Bangalore Technology Center runs AI work combining sensor data, images and VR; India team describes AI building 'new toolboxes and ways of working' (no genAI/coding use named).
Used deep learning, ML, HPC and seismic imaging to identify four new Guyana exploration opportunities (VP Exploration John Ardill).

Infosys expanded collaboration with ExxonMobil on Data Center Immersion Fluids for AI/HPC data centers, using Infosys Topaz (AI) and Cobalt (cloud) - shows an existing Infosys relationship (product-side).
Long-standing Microsoft Azure digital partnership for Permian operations (IoT/cloud).

In-house HPC capability: 'Sr. Principal Technology Architect - HPC, IT Fellow' among ExxonMobil speakers at 2026 Digitalization in Oil and Gas Conference, alongside a Digital Transformation Advisor and OT SOC supervisor.

recent_events.fact: Announced ~2,000 job cuts (3-4% of workforce), concentrated in Canada (Imperial Oil ~half) and EU/Norway, to complete by end-2027; consolidating offices and building a European Technology Center at Antwerp.

Centralization: operations supporting Product Solutions, Low Carbon Solutions and Upstream combined into a single ExxonMobil Global Operations organization in 2026, alongside unified global projects, technology and supply chain organizations.
Raised 2030 plan and structural cost savings target to $20B (from $18B) vs 2019.
CFO Kathy Mikells retired Feb 1, 2026; Neil Hansen (ex-President, Global Business Solutions) became CFO; GBS successor not named in coverage.
Redomiciled from New Jersey to Texas: ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation became the listed parent effective July 1, 2026.
Q2 2026 results lifted by higher oil prices and record Permian output, offsetting Middle East disruptions; $1.08B impairments.
Business transformation 'new system' hub published for partners/suppliers (system and process changes, new system for partner interactions) - consistent with ERP cutover activity.
AI-driven exploration announcement: four new Guyana opportunities identified using AI/HPC.

agent_signals.fact: 65M lines of custom SAP ECC6 code plus a decades-old consolidation mainframe being retired - massive custom-code analysis/remediation and legacy modernization workload through 2028.
12-into-1 ERP consolidation with a 2028 target - integration rewrites, interface migration and testing at scale.

Cybersecurity program managed by the Corporation's VP of Information Technology with cross-functional IT and OT cybersecurity operations managers; Audit Committee does annual cyber review - security reviews of code are a board-visible topic and IT VP is a likely security sponsor.

OT/IT convergence: first live Open Process Automation (OPAS) DCS at Baton Rouge Resins Finishing Plant, cut over end-2024 and running through 2025; second PLC-oriented project at Anchorage Chemical Terminal; goals include reuse of control IP across sites and reduced engineering effort.
Dedicated OT security roles (OT Cybersecurity Expertise Manager; OTCRM SOC Supervisor) presenting at 2026 industry events - mature OT security function to engage on on-call/alert triage.
Cost pressure is explicit and quantified ($20B structural savings target; workforce reductions named as a lever) - productivity tooling must map to this ledger.
Engineering estate signals: Kubernetes, ServiceNow, SailPoint, DevOps secrets engineering; centralized global business centers (Budapest, Bengaluru, Buenos Aires) do shared IT work.
Cloud/data stack: large AWS customer, Snowflake, Celonis on SAP and Salesforce.
10-K lists adopting AI to improve data processing and decision-making as necessary, and AI-enhanced competitors as a risk.

pains: HYPOTHESIS: The 65M-line ECC6 custom-code estate is the critical path to the 2028 S/4HANA target; analyzing, retiring or rewriting ABAP and downstream interfaces is labor-intensive and SI-billed.
HYPOTHESIS: Centralization plus ~2,000 job cuts leaves fewer engineers maintaining the same (or more) applications, creating backlog and key-person risk on legacy systems.
HYPOTHESIS: Mainframe consolidation retirement and integration rewrites need large-scale automated testing and verification that current teams cannot staff.
HYPOTHESIS: Security and IT/OT cyber teams face vulnerability and code-review backlogs across a growing OT software footprint (OPA, containerized control).

HYPOTHESIS: Every new spend must show a line to structural cost savings; the AI program has been process/data-centric (Celonis, Snowflake, Cerebre) and lacks a software-engineering productivity lever.

openers: Of the ~65M lines of ECC6 custom code, how much has been triaged into retire/rewrite/keep, and what does the remaining remediation and testing effort look like against the 2028 cutover?

With the workforce reductions and the move to Global Operations, how are you keeping application maintenance and security backlogs from growing, and does engineering productivity count toward the $20B structural savings ledger?

Where do AI coding assistants sit today (Copilot, Amazon Q, internal), and what would an autonomous agent have to prove in its own sandboxed environment for your IT security and OT teams to let it touch production-adjacent code?

notes: No named CIO/CTO/Chief Digital Officer is published by ExxonMobil; the 10-K refers only to the 'Vice President of Information Technology'. IT leader names (Michael Deal, Bill Keillor, Paolo Biagi, Azmil Ab Aziz) come from a LinkedIn-derived aggregator retrieved Oct 2026 - verify on LinkedIn before outreach. The 'stale' flag uses source date; Curry (2023) and DiTullio (2024-11) are older than 12 months. Neil Hansen's successor as President, Global Business Solutions was not found. Matt Crocker (GBS president 2023-Apr 2025) moved to President, Product Solutions. Revenue figures: company release says $323.9B sales/$332.2B total revenues; LeMondeInformatique says 'nearly $350B' - use the company figure. The 2025 employee number (58k) is from the 10-K; ~2,000 cut program runs to end-2027 so headcount is likely still falling. No public evidence found of GitHub Copilot or a Microsoft EA; a third-party AI tracker lists Microsoft Copilot and IBM Watson without sources (excluded from facts). The Microsoft Azure Permian partnership is 2019 (old). The ARC OPA article date is inferred as 2026 from content ('ran through 2025'). The Sept 2026 'system updates' hub does not name SAP explicitly; link to S/4HANA is inference.
